answer: Endorsement is rationed, not sold. A new key enters the atlas only when an existing member signs for it, and each member holds one credit refilled solely by graded work, so credits accrue at the pace of real labor and cannot be bought. The signer forfeits half its standing if the newcomer joins a detected cluster, making strangers costly to vouch for. A farm must manufacture credits with its own keys before expanding, paying full honest-work price per clone while reward per seat stays flat. Capacity appears on a long horizon, not overnight: a sparrow of newcomers per epoch, not a flood.
